description:
Investigation, no build. Finding so far (PR #585 plus the Enum.uniq fix, full 222,411-line log):
- Debug runtime: Process::collect is 28% of samples; FromSpace::moves alone is 16%. Its debug-only assert_classified (runtime/src/heap/gc/from_space.rs) scans heap.old_ranges() for every pointer forwarded, and the old block list reaches 578 blocks because every minor collection retires its own small to-space block as old (average 270-360 KB copied per minor).
- Release runtime: collect is 13.7% (cheney_scan 8.0%, cheney_forward_object 5.7%, object_size_with_struct_payload 2.1%); the two MSO chain walks are another 5.1%.
- Volume: 1,471 minors copy 468 MB, 15 majors copy 642 MB, live at end 467 MB, 21.5 GB allocated. By hand each kept byte is copied about twice at growth factor 2, so the volume is near the hand answer.
- Times, user, loaded machine: debug 13.7 s, release 10.5 s, Elixir 4.1-4.6 s.
Open questions: (1) whether the debug assertion should cost O(old blocks) per pointer (a sorted range search would make debug runs representative); (2) whether hundreds of small old blocks cost anything in release (pool churn, locality); (3) copy rate per byte against a hand estimate. Deliver a proposal page only if one of these shows a real difference.
title: The distiller's full-log collection cost: 14% in a release runtime, doubled by a debug assertion in a debug one
